title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to -90.0 degrees, 0.0 degrees, and -90.0 degrees, and set the translation vector to [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. The sketch should consist of a closed loop made up of four lines: the first line starts at (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.0235, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.0235, 0.0) and ends at (0.0235, 0.0353); the third line starts at (0.0235, 0.0353) and ends at (0.0, 0.0353); and the fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.0353) and ends at (0.0, 0.0). After drawing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.0353 to the entire sketch. Then, transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it using the Euler angles -90.0 degrees, 0.0 degrees, and -90.0 degrees, and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.75 units in the direction of the normal to create a new solid body. The resulting part has a length of 0.023529411764705875 units, a width of 0.035294117647058816 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0235, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0235, 0.0353) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0353) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
